caption: Piano: F2, A2, C3, E3 at mf, each held 3 s — the tenor’s fast first decay into a long aftersound (round 2 fixed a ×2.2 too-slow prompt decay here)
Piano: C6, E6, G6, C7 at mf, held 2.4 s each — treble unisons kept within a tuner’s beat rate, decaying like the recording instead of collapsing in a beat
Piano: an eight-chord chorale in C minor with legato pedalling — tenor and bass voicing where the decay changes matter most
Violin: D4 forte for 8 s, then A4 for 6 s — the bow runs out of hair and changes direction automatically (cosine reversal, ~70 ms); listen for the turns
Violin: a détaché melody in G — each new note takes the other bow direction (down, up, down…), slurred pairs stay in one bow
Viola: a slow melody on the C and G strings, long notes with bow changes
Cello: C2 and G2 held forte, then an arpeggio up to C4 — bow changes on the long notes, open strings ringing sympathetically
Flute: a low-register phrase at mf (C4–G4) — the strong second harmonic of a real flute’s low notes, from the offset jet and monopole radiation
Flute: G4, G5, G6 each played pp, mf, ff — the tone fills out with the jet as it does on a real flute (fitted to the Iowa recordings)
All five instruments: an original chorale in G for flute, violin, viola, cello and piano (each rendered separately and summed)
Flute: tongued notes in the middle register (A4 C5 E5 A5 G5 E5) — round 3 fixed onsets that took ~4x too long to speak
Piano: the same four chords in a small room (room 0.05), then in a hall (room 0.95) — the round-3 room: image-source early reflections and a 16-line FDN
